title: Short Stuff: Frozen Dead Guy
summary: Short Stuff episode on Brado Morstøl, a Norwegian man whose body was cryonically preserved by his grandson Trygve (Triggvy) Morstøl and grandmother/mother Odd in Nederland, Colorado, and the resulting Frozen Dead Guy Days festival. Covers Brado's death in Norway in 1989, transport to Oakland's TransTime facility, the move to Colorado in 1993 with dry-ice maintenance in a wooden shed, immigration deportation of Trygve in 1994, the town's ordinance and grandfathering, caretaker Bo Schaffer, the shed donated by Tough Sheds, the Chamber of Commerce festival starting in 2002, its 2020 sale to a private entity and move to Sunnyside Park, and Brado's 2023 move to an exhibit at the Stanley Hotel.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Short Stuff episode, with Chuck joking about the frozen body theme and the festival they had mentioned before.

segments.title: Brado Morstøl and the cryonics plan
segments.summary: Brado Morstøl, a Norwegian park designer, died in Norway in 1989 at age 89 without international attention. His grandson Trygve (Triggvy) Morstøl, a cryonics enthusiast, decided to preserve him and planned to build a cryonics facility.

segments.title: Cryonics basics and TransTime
segments.summary: Brado was shipped from Oslo to Oakland, California, where the TransTime cryonics facility kept him in liquid nitrogen for about three years. The hosts explain the goal of cryonics: preserving tissue so people could potentially be revived later.

segments.title: Makeshift freezer in Nederland
segments.summary: In 1993 Trygve, with his mother Odd, moved Brado to a Nederland, Colorado home. Brado was kept in a wooden freezer setup with foam, rubber and dry ice at very cold temperatures, which the hosts say was still inadequate for cryonics. Plans for a concrete structure stalled.

segments.title: Immigration deportation and the festival's origin
segments.summary: Immigration officials ended Trygve's visa and he was deported in 1994, leaving his mother to maintain the dry ice. A local alternative weekly interview with Odd led to news spreading, and the town later created Frozen Dead Guy Days.

segments.title: Town ordinance and grandfathering
segments.summary: The town council found the arrangement was illegal and passed a new ordinance, but Brado was grandfathered in. Trygve also took on a paying customer, Al Campbell, who shared the freezer for a while.

segments.title: Caretaker Bo Schaffer and the donated shed
segments.summary: Trygve advertised for help, and Bo Schaffer maintained the dry ice for thirty years. After a blizzard damaged the shed, a local rock station and Tough Sheds donated a new one, which was painted with the station's classic rock branding.

segments.title: Festival changes and move to Sunnyside Park
segments.summary: The Chamber of Commerce went bankrupt around 2020 and sold the festival rights to a private entity, and the festival moved to Sunnyside Park, losing some of its edge. In August 2023 Brado was moved to the Stanley Hotel.

segments.title: Brado's exhibit at the Stanley Hotel
segments.summary: Brado is now in an exhibit at the Stanley Hotel, sponsored by Alcor, a cryonics company. The hosts joke about where he might go next and about raising money to take custody.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the episode with jokes about classic rock and the show's name, followed by the iHeartRadio production credit.
